```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
# Load the billboard dataset
data("billboard")

# 1. Prepare data
tidy_billboard <- billboard |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("wk"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "rank",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(str_remove(week, "wk")))

# Get Top 10 songs
top_10_songs <- tidy_billboard |>
  group_by(artist, track) |>
  filter(min(rank) <= 10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    # Create a highlight label
    highlight_label = case_when(
      track == "Music" & artist == "Madonna" ~ "Fastest to #1",
      track == "Amazed" & artist == "Lonestar" ~ "Slowest to #1",
      track == "Higher" & artist == "Creed" ~ "Longest Top-10 run",
      TRUE ~ "Other Top-10"
    )
  )

# 2. Plot
ggplot(top_10_songs, aes(x = week, y = rank, group = interaction(artist, track))) +
  # Draw all top-10 songs in gray first
  geom_line(data = filter(top_10_songs, highlight_label == "Other Top-10"), 
            color = "gray80", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Draw the notable songs in color on top
  geom_line(data = filter(top_10_songs, highlight_label != "Other Top-10"), 
            aes(color = highlight_label), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Fastest to #1" = "#E41A1C", 
                                "Slowest to #1" = "#377EB8", 
                                "Longest Top-10 run" = "#4DAF4A")) +
  labs(
    title = "Trajectories of Billboard Top-10 Songs",
    subtitle = "Highlighting notable chart performers",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Rank (Lower is better)",
    color = "Notable Songs"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
